asDecan.p: Your Sun is somewhere in the first ten degrees of Taurus. Every sign splits into three ten-degree decans, each with a planet and a small card, and in the Chaldean order the Golden Dawn used, this opening slice goes to Mercury. Mercury has no special dignity in Taurus. It's a visitor there, neither helped nor held back, so it takes its tone from Venus, who rules the sign. That puts a quick, counting, talkative mind inside fixed earth, a sign that wants to stay put and keep what it has, and the two don't always agree about pace. The next slice along is the Moon's, the Six of Pentacles, which is about giving and receiving. The last is Saturn's, the Seven, waiting for a crop to come in. Yours is the one that does the sums. Look at the picture, two people in the snow walking past a lit window with their heads down. That's the risk with a mind that's always counting. The Hierophant is still your Sun card, and this one fills in the detail.

You know roughly what's in your account without looking, and you look anyway, usually in the queue for coffee. When the price of butter goes up forty cents you notice, and it stays with you for most of the afternoon. When friends split a restaurant bill evenly you work out what you actually ate, and then, nine times out of ten, say nothing. If your boss sends 'got a minute?' late on a Thursday, you've costed losing the job, down to which subscriptions go first, before you've reached their desk. None of that makes you mean. You're often generous, especially with food and time. It's just that Mercury is keeping the books for a sign that likes to feel safe, and the tally rarely switches off. A free Saturday morning tends to end with you on the couch sorting the budget, and you find that oddly calming.

You notice who's struggling, usually well before they say anything. Having enough is never far from your own mind, so you pick it up in other people quickly. A friend suggests a picnic instead of dinner out. A colleague has stopped coming to Friday drinks. A cousin has gone very quiet about the renovation. You clock all of it, and with Venus ruling the sign you tend to deal with it kindly and without any fuss. You're the one who says you over-ordered and could they please take some of this home. You find the cheaper venue for the reunion so the whole group can come, and you never mention why. People who've had a lean year often remember you as the one who made help easy to accept, and some of them only work out years later that you did it on purpose.

Where this slice goes wrong is in bracing for losses that haven't happened, until the bracing costs you more than the loss ever would. I see it a lot with early Taurus Suns. There's a rumour of restructuring at work and you spend three weeks quietly miserable, cancel a holiday, snap at your partner about the power bill, and then the restructure never touches your team. Mercury is quick and Taurus is slow to let go, so a worry gets in fast and then won't leave. And because Mercury likes to talk, the worry leaks into conversation. A friend shows you the new couch and the first thing out of your mouth is what it cost. Someone books a weekend away and you bring up interest rates. You don't mean anything by it, but people notice, and a few of them quietly stop telling you about the nice things they buy.

When something goes wrong, a job lost, a diagnosis in the family, a break-up, your first move is the numbers. You sit down that night and work out how long the savings last, what gets cancelled, what could be sold. That's useful, and it steadies you. A week later is where it gets harder. The sums are done, but you keep doing them, and you start pulling in. You stop answering the group chat because every plan costs money. You say you're fine, because admitting you're short feels worse than being short. The people around you end up guessing, and they usually guess wrong, which leaves them hovering and you feeling watched. What actually helps is one plain conversation with someone you trust where you say the figure out loud, the real one. Then let them do something practical for you, and don't pay them back straight away.

Early on you're slow to let someone pay, and slower still to let them see your bank balance or what's going on with your family's money. People read that as independence. Mostly it's you checking whether it's safe to need them. You show love in practical ways, a full fridge, remembering which tea they drink, fixing the wobbly chair without being asked. With Venus ruling the sign you're affectionate and physical once you settle, but the settling takes a while, and Mercury keeps a quiet count of who gave what the whole time. Partners who do well with you tend to be matter-of-fact about money and generous without making a show of it. The trouble comes if your partner is careless with spending. You won't shout. You'll go cold and start keeping a second, private budget, which is worse.

The Hierophant gives you respect for doing things properly. This slice adds a head for the actual figures. You tend to do well anywhere money, stock or supplies have to be tracked and nobody's allowed to lose any of it. Bookkeeping, procurement, a small shop, a busy kitchen, grant applications, a charity's accounts. Mercury makes you a good negotiator on price, patient and polite and quite hard to move. You're also good at explaining money to people who are frightened of it, which is rarer than it sounds. The usual mistake is underpricing yourself. You'll fight for the company's margin and then accept the first salary offered, because asking for more feels risky. You also tend to stay in a secure job years past the point it suited you. Check the market rate for what you do once a year, and ask for it.

At twenty you're often anxious about money in a way your friends find a bit odd. You're the one with the savings goal and the part-time job, and a fear of being caught short that may or may not match what's actually in the bank. Some people with the Sun here grew up with a real shortage, and some just grew up hearing about one. By the mid-thirties the security usually exists on paper, a deposit saved, steady work, and the question becomes whether you'll let yourself feel it. That's commonly when asking for help gets easier, often after a stretch where you had no choice and found people did turn up. The fifties tend to bring a steadier Taurus, still careful, but able to spend on what you enjoy without justifying it first, and quick to help younger people through their own lean years.

Set aside a small amount each month for spending on nothing useful. It doesn't go to savings or bills or presents for other people. Thirty dollars, fifty, whatever's comfortable. Spend all of it before the month's out on something you enjoy, flowers, a good lunch on your own, a book you'll probably never finish. Don't carry it over. When the voice in your head starts working out what else it could have gone on, let it finish the sum, and buy the thing anyway.
